exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. elective caesarean)
cohort: 104 women (52 vaginal deliveries and 52 elective caesarean sections)
finding: Women who had a vaginal delivery had significantly higher levels of zinc in both maternal and umbilical cord blood, and higher levels of copper in umbilical cord blood, compared to women who had an elective caesarean section.
mod_finding: Women who had a vaginal delivery had significantly higher levels of zinc in both maternal and umbilical cord blood, and higher levels of copper in umbilical cord blood, compared to women who had an elective caesarean section.
